title: A Counterexample to Teschner's Bondage-Number Conjecture
summary: For a finite simple graph $G$ with at least one edge, the bondage number $b(G)$ is the least number of edges whose deletion increases the domination number $γ(G)$. Teschner conjectured that $b(G)\le \tfrac32Δ(G)$ for every graph $G$. We disprove this conjecture by giving a connected cubic bipartite graph on eighteen vertices with \[ γ(G)=6 \qquad\text{and}\qquad b(G)=5. \] The domination number is established by a complete counting argument across the bipartition.
